open_points.subject: confirmation binding and collision handling
open_points.text: A submission whose action, target, version or inputs differ from those the step showed is therefore refused: the digest is a collision-resistant cryptographic digest of one unambiguous encoding of the action, the target, the version and the inputs in that order, every list in its order and an absent value told apart from an empty one, so that two different tuples never share an encoding and digest equality stands for equality of what was shown (round-123 T10).
open_points.question: Does State 2 guarantee refusal only when unequal tuples have unequal digests, with cryptographic collisions outside the guarantee, or must Registry retain enough information to refuse every unequal tuple even when its digest collides?
options: Put collisions outside the guarantee and treat digest equality as computational evidence of equality.
Retain and compare the complete canonical encoding so every unequal tuple is refused even if digests collide.
Require a mathematically collision-free representation instead of a fixed-size cryptographic digest.
open_points.default_guess: Restore the previous collision exclusion and state that digest equality stands for equality only within the collision-resistance assumption.

witness.initial: A session holds a pending confirmation for tuple X, and a distinct tuple Y has the same digest under the selected collision-resistant digest.
events: Registry shows the confirmation step for X and keeps only its digest.
The owner or an attacker submits Y with the pending confirmation value.
outcomes: The differing submission is refused because rule 6 guarantees that every changed action, target, version or input is refused.
The submission passes the binding comparison because Registry keeps no original values and digest(Y) equals digest(X).
witness.observer: The submitting owner and the resulting state change.

open_points.subject: import confirmation mapping bound through A13
open_points.text: The file and the picks are bound by their digest, the names, aliases and Customer values with them, so the mapping it builds is the one the step showed but for the ids production gained in between;
open_points.question: Must an import confirmation be guaranteed to apply the exact file, picks and supplied values shown, even under a digest collision, or is a collision explicitly outside that guarantee?
options: Exclude cryptographic collisions from the guarantee.
Keep and compare the complete bound values or their canonical encoding.
Permit digest equality alone to select the mapping, weakening the claim that it is the mapping shown.
open_points.default_guess: Exclude cryptographic collisions explicitly, consistently with keeping only digests.

witness.initial: Two distinct import selections or input sets have the same binding digest.
events: The owner is shown the mapping for the first input set.
A confirmation carrying the same value is submitted with the second input set.
outcomes: A16 requires the confirming transaction to build and apply the mapping the step showed.
A13's digest-equality check accepts the second input set and the transaction builds its different mapping.
witness.observer: The owner, through the records imported or the refusal details.

open_points.subject: digest algorithm and canonical encoding mechanism
open_points.text: the digest is a collision-resistant cryptographic digest of one unambiguous encoding of the action, the target, the version and the inputs in that order, every list in its order and an absent value told apart from an empty one
open_points.question: Which digest algorithm and exact canonical encoding will generation use for confirmation bindings?
options: SHA-256 over a versioned length-prefixed binary encoding.
SHA-256 over a versioned canonical JSON encoding with explicit type and absence markers.
BLAKE2b-256 over a versioned length-prefixed binary encoding.
open_points.default_guess: SHA-256 over a versioned length-prefixed binary encoding with explicit type, list-order and absent-value markers.
consequences: A binary encoding makes boundaries and types explicit but needs dedicated encoding code and fixtures.
Canonical JSON is easier to inspect but requires fully specified canonicalization, Unicode and numeric rules.
The algorithm choice changes dependency, performance and interoperability characteristics but must not weaken collision resistance.
open_points.requirement: the digest is a collision-resistant cryptographic digest of one unambiguous encoding of the action, the target, the version and the inputs in that order, every list in its order and an absent value told apart from an empty one

set_aside.subject: security-review conclusion for the A13 change
set_aside.text: no right, limit, class or answer moved, and no outcome changed.
set_aside.question: Should the review acknowledge that the guarantee changed from excluding digest collisions to requiring every changed submission to be refused, or should A13 restore the former collision exclusion so that this conclusion remains true?
options: Acknowledge that the required answer changed for a colliding submission and review that change.
Restore the collision exclusion and retain the claim that no answer or outcome changed.
set_aside.default_guess: Restore the collision exclusion; otherwise revise the security-review conclusion.

witness.initial: A pending confirmation's shown tuple and a different submitted tuple share a digest.
events: Under the former text, Registry compares the digests and the collision is outside the guarantee.
Under the current text, the different submission is required to be refused.
outcomes: The former decision permits no guaranteed refusal for this history.
The current decision promises refusal for the same history.

set_aside.subject: representation of monotonic instants
set_aside.text: and its expiry at the latest are held as readings of that monotonic clock
set_aside.question: What representation and precision do monotonic readings use, including the unit and the arithmetic used to add the release durations and decide exact boundary equality?
options: Opaque integer nanoseconds from an unspecified monotonic epoch.
Opaque integer microseconds or milliseconds from an unspecified monotonic epoch.
Floating-point seconds from an unspecified monotonic epoch.
A typed monotonic-instant value whose required precision and comparison semantics are stated without fixing its storage primitive.
set_aside.default_guess: Use a typed monotonic instant backed by integer nanoseconds, with duration addition and exact integer comparison.
set_aside.set_aside_because: an unchanged passage of a unit reviewed for its change

set_aside.subject: number of monotonic readings for an owner request
set_aside.text: Validity is checked when a request arrives (A04 rule 6, stage 1)
set_aside.question: Does an owner request take exactly one monotonic reading at its defined arrival and reuse it for session validity, idle restart and any confirmation shown by that request, or may those decisions take separate readings?
options: Take one arrival reading and reuse it for the session check and new last-request instant; take another only for an event explicitly defined at a later time.
Take separate readings for validity, last-request update and confirmation creation.
Define one operation-wide monotonic reading for every time-dependent result of the request.
set_aside.default_guess: Take one monotonic reading at arrival and reuse it for validity and last-request time, with a later reading only for an event that occurs at a separately defined instant.

witness.initial: A valid session is less than one clock tick from its 30-minute idle boundary.
events: An owner request reaches its defined arrival point before the boundary.
The clock crosses the boundary while Registry performs the session checks and updates.
outcomes: An implementation using the arrival reading serves the request and records that reading as the last request.
An implementation taking a later validity reading refuses the request as idle-expired.
witness.observer: The owner receiving either the requested answer or a sign-in refusal.
